raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Description

`find_free_ports()` currently samples with replacement and stops after `count * 10` attempts. Repeated excluded or occupied candidates can exhaust that budget while eligible free ports remain, which can prevent callers from allocating their service or launcher ports. This patch selects an independent random start and visits each candidate in the configured range at most once, stopping as soon as enough ports are found.

The implementation keeps allocation independent of the training RNG and preserves sorted results. A genuinely exhausted range still raises `ValueError` after all eligible candidates have been checked.

## Related Issue

Fixes #1814

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix
- [ ] ✨ New feature
- [ ] 💥 Breaking change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ♻️ Refactoring
- [ ] ⚡ Performance improvement
- [ ] ✅ Test coverage improvement

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/areal-project/community/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (`pre-commit run --all-files`)
- [x] Relevant tests pass; new tests added for new functionality
- [x] Documentation updated (not applicable; no public API or configuration changes)
- [x] Branch is up to date with `main`
- [x] Self-reviewed via targeted logic and boundary review
- [x] This PR was created by a coding agent via `/create-pr`
- [ ] This PR is a breaking change

## Additional Context

Validation performed against `18f5271f3bf4b78b2a82cf453bbaf75ee0bf8eb6`:

- On the unpatched code, the new deterministic regressions produced 6 failures and 2 passing cases.
- `python -m pytest tests/test_network_ipv6_utils.py -q -rs`: **20 passed, 2 skipped** (IPv4-only and IPv6-only route checks are skipped on this host).
- An independent exhaustive oracle over 7,290 five-port availability/exclusion/start/count combinations passed.
- 20 real socket smoke trials passed: an occupied starting port was skipped, and selected ports accepted both TCP and UDP binds.
- `python -m compileall -q areal/utils/network.py tests/test_network_ipv6_utils.py`: passed.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: all hooks passed, including Ruff, CLI documentation generation, lockfile consistency, and SPDX. The commit-time Conventional Commits hook also passed.
- The commit includes a DCO sign-off.

Risk and validation scope: exhausted or densely occupied ranges can require more socket probes than the old heuristic, up to one per eligible candidate. The existing check/bind TOCTOU window remains; this change does not reserve the returned ports. No Docker or GPU/distributed training suite was run for this standard-library utility fix.

files.patch:
@@ -158,45 +158,45 @@ def find_free_ports(
 
     min_port, max_port = port_range
     free_ports = []
-    attempted_ports = set()
+    range_size = max_port - min_port + 1
 
     # Calculate available port range. Only excluded ports that fall within
     # [min_port, max_port] reduce availability; out-of-range entries do not.
     in_range_excluded = sum(min_port <= p <= max_port for p in exclude_ports)
-    available_range = max_port - min_port + 1 - in_range_excluded
+    available_range = range_size - in_range_excluded
 
     if count > available_range:
         raise ValueError(
             f"Cannot find {count} ports in range {port_range}. "
             f"Only {available_range} ports available."
         )
 
-    max_attempts = count * 10  # Reasonable limit to avoid infinite loops
+    if count <= 0:
+        return []
+
     attempts = 0
     # Network resources must not follow or advance the training RNG: jobs with
     # the same training seed otherwise compete for the same port sequence.
     port_rng = random.SystemRandom()
+    start_port = port_rng.randint(min_port, max_port)
 
-    while len(free_ports) < count and attempts < max_attempts:
-        # Generate random port within range
-        port = port_rng.randint(min_port, max_port)
-
-        # Skip if port already attempted or excluded
-        if port in attempted_ports or port in exclude_ports:
-            attempts += 1
+    # Walk the range once, wrapping around at max_port. Repeated random draws
+    # can exhaust a retry budget even when unattempted free ports remain.
+    for offset in range(range_size):
+        port = min_port + (start_port - min_port + offset) % range_size
+        if port in exclude_ports:
             continue
 
-        attempted_ports.add(port)
-
+        attempts += 1
         if is_port_free(port):
             free_ports.append(port)
-
-        attempts += 1
+            if len(free_ports) == count:
+                break
 
     if len(free_ports) < count:
         raise ValueError(
             f"Could only find {len(free_ports)} free ports "
-            f"out of {count} requested after {max_attempts} attempts"
+            f"out of {count} requested after {attempts} attempts"
         )
 
     return sorted(free_ports)

@@ -166,3 +166,68 @@ def test_find_free_ports_seeded_candidates_busy_uses_independent_rng(monkeypatch
 
     assert network.find_free_ports(1) == [free_port]
     assert training_rng.getstate() == state
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("occupied", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("start_port", [10000, 10010, 10020])
+def test_find_free_ports_sparse_availability_returns_remaining_port(
+    monkeypatch, occupied, start_port
+):
+    """Find a sole eligible port regardless of the random starting point."""
+    network = _load_network_module()
+    free_port = 10010
+    unavailable = set(range(10000, 10021)) - {free_port}
+    checked = []
+
+    def is_port_free(port):
+        checked.append(port)
+        return port == free_port
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        network.random.SystemRandom, "randint", lambda self, lo, hi: start_port
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(network, "is_port_free", is_port_free)
+
+    assert network.find_free_ports(
+        1, (10000, 10020), exclude_ports=set() if occupied else unavailable
+    ) == [free_port]
+    assert len(checked) == len(set(checked))
+    if not occupied:
+        assert checked == [free_port]
+
+
+def test_find_free_ports_full_range_returns_sorted_unique_ports(monkeypatch):
+    """Repeated random draws must not prevent filling an entirely free range."""
+    network = _load_network_module()
+    checked = []
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        network.random.SystemRandom, "randint", lambda self, lo, hi: 10003
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        network, "is_port_free", lambda port: checked.append(port) or True
+    )
+
+    assert network.find_free_ports(6, (10000, 10005)) == list(range(10000, 10006))
+    assert len(checked) == len(set(checked)) == 6
+
+
+def test_find_free_ports_exhausted_range_checks_all_eligible_ports_once(monkeypatch):
+    """Report insufficient free ports only after inspecting every candidate."""
+    network = _load_network_module()
+    excluded = {10001, 10004}
+    checked = []
+
+    def is_port_free(port):
+        checked.append(port)
+        return port == 10003
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        network.random.SystemRandom, "randint", lambda self, lo, hi: 10003
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(network, "is_port_free", is_port_free)
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Could only find 1 free ports out of 2"):
+        network.find_free_ports(2, (10000, 10005), exclude_ports=excluded)
+
+    assert set(checked) == set(range(10000, 10006)) - excluded
+    assert len(checked) == len(set(checked))
